utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, good afternoon everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, The Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearance, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honour, learned counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Kyle Wood for the Prosecution assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic-Ivanov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon to my colleagues from the Prosecution, to everyone in the courtroom and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the accused and legal assistant Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony yesterday you made a declaration to tell the truth the whole truth and nothing else but the truth. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I take this opportunity to remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General Karavelic. I hope you have had a good rest and that we can continue today where we left off yesterday. We have been discussing the problems you had with certain units. We also discussed the Presidency and the use of force, and I wish to develop that subject today, to meet also the request of Honourable Judge Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at Exhibit number 9, please. For the record, it is a decree law on the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, adopted on the 20th of May, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will now provide a clarification. It was promulgated in November as indicated above the title, but I will ask for a moment to move to the last page in Bosnian and the last page in English. The decree law was enacted, it says in Article 43. This decree law enters into force immediately and shall be promulgated in the Official Gazette, 20th May, 1992. It was adopted in May, and it was published in November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now ask the legal officer to take us back to the first page and zoom in on Article 8 and 9. Page 2 of the English version. We can already see it in Bosnian. We need page 2 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at Article 8, and then Article 9, focussing on item 5. Before I ask your comment, did you hold this decree law in your hands at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now look at Article 8. I will quote this single sentence: "The Presidency of the Republic shall be the highest body of the command and control of the army." And then Article 9, item 5: "Shall determine the plan of employment of the army in the event of war and order the employment of the army in peacetime and war." Could you briefly comment upon these?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the document says, the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was the highest command of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the army. The item 5 explicitly says that for any kind of employment of the army in peacetime and in war, in other words, for the use of armed force it is precisely that body, the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as the Supreme Command that is responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You described yesterday a situation that you had involving disobedient units and on that occasion you addressed, you approached, the Presidency and the president himself, Mr. Izetbegovic. Who had the authority, who was the one who should have requested the use of force in that situation?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that situation, the commander of the corps. That is me, and I did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now look at Exhibit 218, under seal. We would need to move into private session. I would like to question the witness on this and the next exhibit in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to show Exhibit 959 to the witness next. For the record, there is minutes of the council for the protection of constitutional order held on the 24th of November, 1993. Could we please display the English version so that we can see the whole page at once. Could the witness see page 3, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Just to point an of clarification, Your Honour, there does appear to be a discrepancy at the top it says 24 November 1993 but it -- in the body of the text it says held on 28 October 1993. This is something that should perhaps be clarified before Defence counsel goes further with this document, or at the very least corrected in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the discrepancy, Mr. Wood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Well, in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have told us the different dates but what is the discrepancy in those dates? You mean you can't report on the 24th about a meeting that took place on the 28th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Certainly, but what the record reflects right now is that this meeting was held on the 24th of November 1993 and that is not what the body of the text actually reflects this is dated 24 November 1993 line 5, page 15, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, that is something with the record. That's nothing to do with the exhibit itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it has to do with the record, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, so the record -- maybe she misspoke that, I don't know. She can explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, but there is nothing wrong with the document as it stands before us. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at page 3, item 5. It is page 3 in the English as well. Witness, Mr. Karavelic, your name is mentioned in item 5. Is it you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Mr. Vahid Karavelic, the 1st Corps commander, stated that the operation had been successful and although it was called for sooner, there had been no political will to do so." First and foremost I would like to ask you the following: As you can see it was a meeting of the council for the protection of the constitutional order. Did you attend any such meetings and tell us whether there reflects the discussion at that particular meeting, if you were in attendance?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended several such meetings. This part that you referred to reflects the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are quoted as having said that some were asking for the action or operation to be undertaken earlier but that there was no political will. Can you explain to us what it means?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means ... as I said yesterday, as of May 1993, the 1st Corps command was demanding that disobedient commanders be replaced. As time went on, the situation grew worse. We kept repeating our demands, asking for it to be done at any time, but what was missing was the key decision that was supposed to be made by the president of the Presidency of B&H as the Supreme Commander. Therefore, the operation could not take place before the 26th October 1993, when, finally, he approved it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, just a little interruption it has been partly corrected on two occasions the interpretation has interpreted that the word "decision" in paragraph 5 of this document as "will." It is only now finally that the word decision has been mentioned by the interpretation. Was it political will or political decision that was lacking.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Decision, Your Honour. It is very clearly stated in the document, "decision."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand it is just that the interpretation on two occasions has talked of "will." Thank you very much. Decision, we know it's "decision" now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's just clarify one more thing. What were you talking about, the political will or a political decision?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness now please be shown Exhibit 959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Political decision was made by the Presidency or by the president himself? That's a question I want to ask.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will call for a longish answer. When I, in mid-October 1993, at my insistence when I finally went to see President Izetbegovic and when he received me, I told him, Mr. President, you have appointed me as commander, corps commander, two months ago, or a bit longer, if you do not issue in writing as soon as possible that I can use any type of armed force in order to bring the chain of command and the commanding in the corps in -- to a normal level I cannot accept to continue in this position as commander of the 1st Corps. And then he answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was long conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please don't tell us the details of that. Was the decision made by the president of the Presidency or was it made by the Presidency? Just answer that part of it. We haven't got much time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would have been my -- the next thing I was going to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who made the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then he told me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was the Presidency of the Supreme Command that they made this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now please see Exhibit D555. I apologise, D955. Your Honour, unfortunately, this is the Official Gazette that we had in electronic form. It is a bit dark. But in fact, it is only the title that will is blacked out. This is an decree law on amendments to the decree Law on the Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us, have you had occasion to see this decree law? Have I shown this to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see this during the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to point to you to Article 2 of this decree law. Would you please read it. General, could you please comment on this? What is stipulated by Article 2 here?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 2 of this decree stipulates that the Supreme Command may, for a portion of their work, of the work that is to be carried out by units of the civilian police, that the Supreme Command may, for some of those jobs, use also units of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please have a number, an Exhibit number for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become exhibit number 1335.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Can I just ask one little question before we go further, just for clarification. General, you say that you went to talk to the president of the Presidency. Did the chain of command not demand that you speak to the General -- to the commander of the army and that he speaks to the president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely right. And I did speak with the army commander a number of times, on numerous occasions, and I also believed that the army commander had spoke -- talked to President Izetbegovic. However, at this time, when I had this meeting with President Izetbegovic, this was actually -- this culminated the situation because I was issued threats, threats to the effect that I will be put on the spit, and at this point I decided to go and see the commander, because at -- at this point I went to see him, because the commander was not in town at that time. Or maybe it was with his permission. I cannot really remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, just a few more questions that have to do with the situation with Celo and Caco. During your testimony, you mentioned that the commanders of these two renegade brigades did not enjoy the support of all members of its brigades. Could you tell us, the percentage of people, approximately, who supported these commanders?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true, these commanders did not enjoy the support of the entire complements. I can say that approximately one-fourth of the ranks in their brigades had supported them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you this. By how you judge the atmosphere in Sarajevo when these units were concerned, what was the position in the city, in terms of support for these renegade units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, it was negative and a very small percentage, a very small number of people supported them, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another question. So the 1st Corps carried out this operation. How many soldiers did it use in this showdown; do you recall? Which forces attacked these units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, of course. I used up to 5.000 men, and these 5.000 men were men from my corps alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to these forces from your corps, were there any other forces that were involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Units of the Ministry of Interior; in other words, civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of those units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were about 500 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that as the first superior of these recalcitrant unit, disobedient units, that you demanded the use of force. Tell me, what are those occasions where you can actually ask for the use of force? Why did you ask for this and at what point in time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The use of the armed force, in my view, is called for in the event of large-scale war crimes in the event of large-scale violations or disturbance of the peace or violations of rights and in those cases where such instances cannot be resolved by disciplinary measures alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to do this to you Madam Vidovic. What was the strength of the renegade units. How many soldiers approximately would you say they had, those who supported the renegades, those against whom the 5.500 had to fight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will have to add it up. To make it clearer, there were units that we were attacking. Then there were other units that we did not trust, and we were afraid that they might try and support them and attack us from the back. All those units, this entire complement, or ranks, numbered approximately between 2 and 3.000 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know how many of them were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 18 men. There were also a number of wounded people, a large number of wounded people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the rest surrendered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rest we took prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But Celo and Caco were killed in the operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only Caco was killed. Celo was not killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just go back -- let's backtrack a bit. You told us that the use of force is called for in situations where there is large-scale violation or disturbance of the peace, violations of peace and discipline and war crimes. Does this include minor infringements or infractions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, infractions are regulated by disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I think the witness said large-scale war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General Karavelic, tell me, please, what were the neighbouring corps, neighbouring to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps next to mine were the 2nd Tuzla Corps; the 3rd Zenica Corps; and the 4th Mostar Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know what the overall situation was in the neighbouring corps; for instance in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you said well, I did know the overall or global situation more or less. I was familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long the lines of the 3rd Corps were compared to your front lines? Could you describe this a bit?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my lines -- my front lines were considered to be rather long. However, the lines of the 3rd Corps, the defence lines of the 3rd Corps, were by far the longest, compared to any other corps in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you make a comparison between the defence lines of your corps and the defence lines held by the 3rd Corps? What would be the ratio?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Length-wise, I believe the 3rd Corps had double the length of defence line of my corps, and I had double the strength of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In terms of manpower, I suppose, or also in terms of artillery and weaponry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same. The level of armament varied very little from corps to corps. Every effort was made to distribute weapons evenly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. So you had the same artillery but double the number of soldiers at your disposal, compared to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the impression the Chamber had questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General Karavelic, you testified that you had been through a very difficult situation when you had to establish discipline in your units. Throughout that time, what attitude did General Delic take to this issue, establishing discipline in units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying this with absolute certainty, from his first day as top man in the army, he firmly required that anyone who was not within the chain of command be removed, anyone who did not follow army regulations and observe army discipline, from his very first day to his last day in the army, he invested every effort to build up discipline. But it was a process, and for that process to move faster, a political decision was required, a decision made from the highest command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do you know if, regarding this attitude of his, do you know if General Delic asked the Presidency to issue a political decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, I recall, he did ask, on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And he never obtained a political decision? Always, of course, in support of his attitude with his will to get rid of all the people who did not obey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot say now whether he ever got it or not, but I know that most times he did not get any reply from the highest command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So how do you know this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, specifically, I believe we saw a document, it was earlier today or yesterday, from a meeting in Zenica, from a conference, where it was General Delic who raised a couple of issues that were within the jurisdiction of the Supreme Command, and I know that for a long time afterwards he did not get any reply from the Supreme Command, although he submitted his requests to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we will see this document. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just let us clarify one thing. You mentioned the highest command several times. You said a political decision had to be made by the highest command. What did you mean by "the highest command"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was, militarily speaking, called the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I think we can manage one more document before the break, Exhibit 1248. It is, for the record, a document from the Supreme Command of armed forces, dated 29 August 1993. The title is: Conclusions and tasks adopted at the meeting of senior officers of the Main Staff and corps commanders, held in Zenica on 21 and 22 August 1993. Witness, General, could you please look at the passage where all the people from the corps are indicated as present. Do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend that conference?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we scroll the document down to see the rest of the text. And then if we could move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on item 7 on this page. When you've read it, please give us your comments.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item 7 mentions, in terms of this conference on training and discipline, that the staff commander speaks openly of problems that we encountered at every level in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as far as lack of discipline is concerned and lack of military training of both officers and soldiers. Speaking of training, he calls for ongoing training of squad commanders and company commanders, because these units are the basic units in armed combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 4 of both English and Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to item 9. Could you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if there was any mention that meeting of independent units that were out of control?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, and at this point could we look at item 10, what conclusions was made in relation to these independent units -- units; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do. The conclusion made was that these independent units should be, at all costs, assigned so various units of the corps, so that they could be placed under control more easily in the period that followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify one aspect of the answer you've just given. The reference here is to smaller independent units that should be assigned, distributed across the corps. Could you explain to us with no military knowledge why this was to be done? Why a small unit should be integrated into the corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to military rules, the staff commander deals with the corps commander, and it is up to the corps commander to fulfil whatever request he received from above and do the actual integration of smaller units within the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But who decides on the employment of such units in combat?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, of course, it is the corps commander, or the commander who received that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to make sure we are absolutely clear. The transcript talks of staff commander is that a reference to the commander of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us clarify with the witness one thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I said what I asked you was who decides on the further assignment of these forces?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because we have in the transcript something that is not clear. Yes, because the term "employment" is used.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the counsel ignores the actual meaning of employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who decides on the further employment of these units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the corps and the lower commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really don't understand what's going on. I keep saying who is deciding on the use and I cannot believe that what's in the transcript is correct. I want the word "use," not "employment" used.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, General, let me ask you again. Who asks about the further use of these units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander and the commanders below him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient point?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to resolve this, I really cannot understand this. At certain points in certain passages I repeat certain rather simple words, words that are simple to translate from Bosnian into English, such as the word "use," and repeatedly here we get another word, like "employment." Could you please draw the attention of the interpreters or whoever who is typing over there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought at line -- on page 29, lines 6 to 9 that has now been corrected, Madam Vidovic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot say but I'm talking about this last line -- which one, Your Honour? I didn't see but what I'm saying is that the word deployment is completely -- is sometimes confused with the word employment. And I -- after this session, I will ask for the audiotape to be reviewed and the transcript to be corrected, not to waste time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. My question to you had been, Would this be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's take a break and start afresh at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to show the witness document number 1069. For the record, it is a work plan of the Supreme Command Staff for December 1993. Your Honours, we have an illegible version in e-court, but we strove to have a clean version in hard copy. I would kindly ask the usher to show it to the Prosecution first and then to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then use the ELMO, Madam Vidovic, now that the witness is going to use that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's the B/C/S version. Okay. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. For the record, it is a work plan of the RB and H armed force Supreme Command Staff for December 1993. I would kindly ask the witness to have a look at page 7 of the document. It is page 5 in the English version. 7 in B/C/S; and 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any point specifically on that page, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would kindly ask the witness to have a look at 7.2. You can see it as well. As well as item 8.4. It is also on this page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that on page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version it will be page 6, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just scroll down so that we can see 8.4 in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In our version, we have it as copied. Please find 7.2. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is mentioned is a development of a new temporary war formation OG as well as visit and review of the situation in Branches and corps and taking of measures to improve the situation. On this page, we can see that all corps were given this task. Can you comment upon this part of the document. You saw that it refers to December 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until that point, we had operational groups as part of the corps, corps, and, as such, the war formations were becoming obsolete, in a sense they could no longer respond to the needs in the field; therefore, we initiated the establishment of new war formations for operative groups which at the same time provided basis to form divisions instead of operational groups in early 1994. That is the gist of item 7.2. As for 8.4, there was a frequent task in different periods, including visits and reviews of the situation in branchs and corps and that would usually be undertaken by the General Staff through its administrations that would go in the field in order to carry out checks in the various branches and units of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also receive such a task for your corps, to review the situation in your units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to go to page 3 of the document. It is also page 3 in the English. Witness, in your copy, it is 3.3. The title of the chapter; security administration, and then have you item 3.3.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is mentioned is a certain operation. It terms of what you know, tell us whether certain activities in the units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina when it comes to resolving the situation with those who were disobedient, was such a situation limited only to the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such a situation existed in all corps, including other parts of the free territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the code-name was for that operation, or operations?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trebevic 2, 3, 4, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please give an exhibit number to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be become Exhibit number 1336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, I was unsure of the relevance of this document. Could you enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd be happy to, Your Honour. The last item is relevant for two reasons. Firstly, because measures were being taken in order to resolve the situation in the corps as of late 1993 onwards; secondly, what is being ordered is to continue with the Trebevic-3 operation. As we heard so far, in December 1993, the Trebevic-3 operation was initiated in the area of Zenica. We had several witnesses testify about that, and orders were issued to continue with that operation. If you can recall that. Perhaps I can clarify further. We had some Prosecution witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I remember perfectly well, but the fact that there was an order to continue that operation shows what exactly? I mean, it show that the operation was continued, yes; and so what?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you remember, a witness of the Prosecution, he said that that operation was stopped significantly before that time. As for its continuation, it was partially aimed at the Gerila which had been driven out, as part of the Trebevic-3 operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I did not begin testifying myself. I don't know whether I asked for an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, you did, ma'am, and it is Exhibit 1336.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General Karavelic, on to a different topic now. You told us you were a corps commander between July 1993 and up to a concern point in 1995. We are yet to arrive at that point. But as the corps commander, did you use the manual or the rule book on military discipline?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a look at Exhibit 1240 next. For the record, it is a document from the Ministry of Defence, Sarajevo, dated 19th January 1993, sent to the 3rd Corps. I will not ask you whether you have seen this document or not; rather, I will ask you about a part of this document in trying to ascertain what was actually happening in practice. I will quote the last part of the document. Could you please scroll up in the English version so that the Bench can follow. There is just one portion of the text. Once I'm through with the first sentence in Bosnian, I would kindly ask to you go over to the next page in English. However, following the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency decision of the 18th of August 1992 on the formation of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina army corps their zones of responsibility and subordination of the strict defence staffs to army corps command, the corps commander is the only officer who has the right and duty to issue decisions to bring those who commit violations before a military disciplinary court. I wanted to ask you this: The sentence I read out, was it implemented, was it put into practice in 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the competent officer or superior to submit a report against a perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that the witness be shown D940 next.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to discuss the measures taken within the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D940. It is a document of the Supreme Command Staff of the 14th of July, 1993. The title is: Order on elimination of weaknesses displayed in mobilisation and release of soldiers and MTS in the war units of the army of the Republic of B&H.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you read the document on the screen or would you rather have us zoom in on the first paragraph of the document in the Bosnian. That's the part. Yes, thank you. We can see it better now. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on item 1 of the order. Perhaps it is easier if I quote. It says: "To all commands, staffs, units and institutions of the RB&H army, I hereby prohibit immediate-direct mobilisation or deployment of conscripts and MTS organised by themselves. Staffing of war units of the army on all levels of commands and control is to be done exclusively by requests through relevant defence secretariats with strict abidance by the legal provisions stipulated by the decree on criteria and regulations for assignment of citizens and material equipment to the armed force and other defence needs." Let us go to page 2 of the document in both versions, item 7, and following that, I will seek your comment. It is a bit difficult to read there Bosnian. I will quote. Item 7 says: "I hereby prohibit direct admittance of recruits, volunteers to war units, and the existing recruits, volunteers in war units are to be treated in accordance with point 4 of this staff's order ..." I wanted to ask you this. You said that have you seen this order before. I want to ask you whether you received it and whether the corps were duty-bound to implement it, and that should include all the units of the army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received it, and we were duty-bound to implement it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Madam Vidovic, but it was not addressed to your corps, sir? How did you see it? It was not addressed to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let him tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I used to receive such orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But go to page 1 of that document. Can we go to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please zoom in on the right-hand side in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, please. Can we go to page 1 in the English as well, please. Look at the addressees there, to commands of 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th corps. Yours is not one of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In front of the 2, there is a 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In front of the English 2 there is a question mark. Can we enlarge the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Use the magnifier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, scroll down, please. Down. Down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, the other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The other way. Thank you. Hold it there. Thank you very much. We can see what we see there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But can you magnify -- the letter 2. Yes. Do it again, please. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this, General Karavelic. In practice, were the corps and the units below them duty-bound to implement the order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask for an exhibit number for the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: There are a number of problems. Apparently with the translation of this document. Your Honour the first which was pointed out it doesn't appear to have been sent. It is an ambiguous to mark before the 1 -- before the 2. But a larger issue is there is text that appears to be scratched out in the B/C/S version and that doesn't appear on the English version. Additionally there is some handwritten text at the bottom of the document on the last page that also does not appear to have been translated, and I would just ask that a proper translation be provided before this is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just have to see what my colleague is referring to. In the Bosnian version, I don't see -- all right, now I see what he means. This part is scratched out. I don't quite understand what's the problem with this scratched out version? Perhaps the Prosecutor may enlighten me. Your Honour, this is an official translation of the document. We were not the ones who translated it. But I don't see what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the problem is that the two are not identical. The one has writing on it which is scratched out. The other one has no similar writing. There's nothing written below the corps there in the English translation, which is scratched out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And it is not known why it is scratched out. I'm just telling you what the Prosecutor is saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour, I accept that. But, secondly, the English translation has a third page also where everything that was handwritten on the original version was translated. Perhaps my colleague can see it now. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I see that now, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your colleague can see it now. Can we go back to page 1 in the English, please. Now, sorry, can we just hold on that to -- can we see the last page of -- of the B/C/S, please. Yes. You see both the handwritten part and the translation don't show the 1st Corps. So we are told here who it was sent to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness clarify it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any idea why -- let's see if we can check the Bosnian version. So do you have any idea or what the meaning of this CVO et cetera and then forwarded to, what does that -- that portion, what does that mean? And why is the 1st Corps not mentioned here, whereas it was on the first page? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Here the CVK and the KZ that means encrypted, and then below that it says forwarded to, and then the corps that received an encrypted version were mentioned there so only those corps that received a document in encrypted form are listed here; and as for my corps, I received this in an envelope because my command is close to a command in the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. I have now forgotten what I wanted at page 1, so we can go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we go back to the first page, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we may.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can see the first page of the document again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, I do remember what it is I wanted to say. Can we scroll down the B/C/S slightly, please -- I beg your pardon, scroll up. Can we do the same with the English. Now, there are faint handwritten writings on the top of the B/C/S, which we don't see on the top of the English. There's what looks like a 5 right on top, and then a little string of numbers and then something encircled. Are we able to decipher that, the handwritten parts? Are you able to do that, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, the first number is 31-2-03-362-4/4-5/39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is possible too. It's possible that it is 99.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And would that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, this is the record of the document in our archives, in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or, rather, in the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And what looks like a 5 circled on top, would that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say. It doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is circled below, does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only say that this too doesn't seem to make any sense, but sometimes individuals would just put their own markings on a document that have no meaning whatsoever. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to ask from the witness. Is it possible that this document was not sent to the 1st Corps, because it refers to a meeting during which there were also the representatives of the 1st Corps. That's what I could understand. Maybe I'm wrong, but that's what I would understand from the first paragraph of the document. It was a meeting, working meeting, of the representatives of the government of the Republic, the Ministry of Defence of the secretariat of Defence in the district of Sarajevo, and - how do you say? - the Supreme Commander of the Main Staff, and the 1st Corps. Therefore, this is probably the reason why it wasn't sent to the 1st Corps. It's an explanation, isn't it to solve this problem, to understand why it was not sent to the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was not the practice. It does not correspond to the military rules of correspond. Whether someone was at the meeting or not, they would still have to receive the same because this document describes the tasks and duties over a long period of time; so that I had to receive this document, I'm absolutely certain of it, 100 percent. There's no dilemma about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you certain that you had to receive it, or are you certain that you did receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received -- I did receive it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. My very last question. Are you able to decipher the words that are struck out in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it says there to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then in parenthesis: For your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please have a number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, could the witness be shown D942. Your Honour, before the document is displayed, we will seek to amend the document with -- to replace the previous document where this portion was scratched out, we will provide another version with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this document, D942, is from the Main Staff of the armed forces of the 3rd of August, 1993, and it's entitled: Order. Could we please see the bottom of the document. Can you just show it so that we can see the whole thing. Thank you. And the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do you see the date, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the reasons I asked for the bottom of the document to be displayed is because there is mention made in several places there at the 3rd of August, and I will ask the witness to explain there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3rd August 1993 is also mentioned in the preamble of this document, before the word "order." Plus in handwriting at the bottom of the document where we see that it was sent as an encrypted document, there is the date 3rd August 1993, and the hour when the document was sent to the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you seen and received this document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document is short. Would you please take a look at it and perhaps give your comments on it. What did it refer to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the orders from the commander of the Main Staff -- the General Staff for a sort of cease-fire, and there were many of those in the four years of the war, and here the -- it is ordered that the subordinates, us, the corps commanders, are to strictly comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at items 5 and 7. What do they deal with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 5 orders that all the military units are to fully protect civilian population -- the civilian population or civilians. And in item 6 it says that the corps commanders shall be personally responsible for the consistent implementation of this order and in case of violation of this order, this Staff is to be informed immediately. By staff they mean the Main Staff, the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become exhibit number 1338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now see document D1068. Your Honour, in the electronic version, we have a bad copy. This is how we received it from the Prosecution. However, it appears that the hard copy is better, and I would appreciate if the usher could show this to the Prosecutor and then to the witness. For the record, let me say that this is a document from the morale administration of 26th June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, would you please look at the first page. Have I shown you this document in preparation for this trial?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How would you comment what is in the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Question. Okay, how much time? A couple minutes? Should we then take a break? I think so. Take a break and we will be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's hope we can get on now. Madam Vidovic. Sorry about that break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope, General, that you had the opportunity to read this document. I noticed that during the break you had it in your hands. I'm talking about the document of the staff of the Supreme Command, D1068, of the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can just wait for it. Thank you very much. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had the opportunity to read it. Could you tell us, what does it deal with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document says that the General Staff received from the Institute for War Crimes that had been established by that time in Sarajevo that they should do something to improve the method of fact-finding related to war crimes, among other things, the chief of the administration for morale at the General Staff, Mr. Ivan Brigic, is sending a letter with several suggestions as to what should be done. And he is sending it to the commander of the staff of the Supreme Command of armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you stop there, because I want to move to the next page for my next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page in Bosnian and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just lower the page. The handwriting is not legible entirely, but I hope you have managed to make it out. Do you agree that this handwritten passage is related to the corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does it say?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the commander of the General Staff agrees to have consultations with a number of representatives of the institute to find the best mode, the best way, and, furthermore, the commander says that it would be then applied while keeping the existing services in commands and units and that they should do that job.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, as corps commander, receive an instruction that you should collect information about war crimes during combat activities, if any war crimes had taken place?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received such documents on more than one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were those orders issued to all corps or just the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are very few documents addressed to the 1st Corps alone. I meant all the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get a number, Your Honours, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1339.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness now look at D373.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for that document, Mr. Karavelic, I would be curious to know if indeed the methods that were recommended by General Delic were ever implemented in practice; do you know? The instructions that he gave on the document that we have just seen on the screen, were they ever complied with, in practice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there were a great number of documents at the higher level of command were drafted and sent down to units. Implementation is a different matter. It depended on what kind of officers we had at lower levels of command, how well trained and how competent they were, how qualified, and how prepared they were to deal with all the orders received from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sure Mrs. Vidovic will pursue this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Still, General, I suppose you can't speak for other corps, but speaking of your own, did you actually have that practice in the 1st Corps? If you found out, for instance, about war crimes, in the 1st Corps, did you collect data about that? I don't mean you personally; I mean your security service.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my service did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your service file any criminal reports in that regard?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would now like to see document D373, which we have here. It is a document from the office of the commander of the staff of supreme staff of the 26th of November, 1993. It is called order to comply with the Geneva Convention.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, General, have you seen this document before? Did you receive it then?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is this document, briefly?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, the document insists on compliance with the Geneva Convention in treatment of civilian population and prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did receive this document. When you received this document, did it remain in your drawer or did you send it down?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single document received from the General Staff remains in -- on my desk. The commander who received it adds to it, whatever he sees fit, and then sends it down to commanders of divisions, brigades, battalion, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have an Exhibit number for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know -- I don't know who to put my question to you. Maybe to -- since -- okay, I put it directly to the witness directly then. Mr. Karavelic, what prompted this letter; do you know? My question is: What prompted the ICRC to -- to address itself to the ABiH and ask for a report on prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says in the first part of this document what prompted it, the first three lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain, General?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have received from the International Committee of the Red Cross a report about the employment of prisoners of war for works conducted in conditions hazardous for their lives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And, so, I assume that there has been an incident in which the ICRC has come across prisoners of war who have been used in dangerous work, in violation of the Geneva Conventions. And that was what my question was about: What was that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell you that, not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1340.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness please look at D977. For the record, this is a document from the staff of the Supreme Command dated 27th December 1994. The title is: Tasks related to command and control. Do you see, General, in the right top corner, to whom it was sent?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive it during the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 6 on this page. The English version should be shown on page 2 where item 6 is. General, let me ask you this: What does this document relate to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document relates to the tasks issued by the General Staff solely in the domain of control and command, over the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now look at page 5 of this document, pages 6 and 7 in English. Page 5 in Bosnian, and page 6 and 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at items 6 through 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how I'll deal with it. When the Judges finish reading page 6, we should move to page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please comment, especially on item 6. It says: "Do not keep any documentation on war crimes in units; send it all to the military security administration, to the specialised section for this type of work, in cooperation with the MUP engage military police units and ensure full control of free territory." "Ensure the highest quality and most comprehensive possible work of SVB members with the goal of detecting all forms of criminal activities and their perpetrators in the army of BH through the implementation of the Trebevic operation and other regular activities of SVB and military police members." What I want to ask you is this: We saw earlier a document ordering compliance with Geneva Conventions. How would you qualify this document? What does it deal with in point 6 through 13?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows up on the previous document related to Geneva Conventions. It Stipulates that every officer in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the highest to the lowest level in the event he learns of a war crime that was perpetrated or any other serious violation of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an Exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document becomes Exhibit number 1341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the witness now to see document D988. While we're waiting for the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, can I ask you this: Earlier in your evidence you said there were few trained and professional officers, and you said certain efforts were made to improve that situation from mid-1993 until the end of the war. Tell me, what did this cover? What kind of efforts were these?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the General Staff issued various orders for that purpose, plus it sent its best and most qualified officers to conduct training in lower units of the corps and it also carried out the general training for soldiers and officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have here an order from 1995. I would like to move to page 2, para 1. Page 2 in Bosnian and English. Could you look at para 1 and then 3 and 4. And tell us when you finish reading what this document is about. But, first of all, did you receive it at the time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. A truce, a cease-fire must have been signed prior to this document, and the commander appears to be using that time to devote maximum attention to training, training of the commands, officers, units, and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this something exceptional that you received such an order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were similar orders before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an Exhibit number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show witness D990 next, please. This will another illegible version in e-court. Therefore, I would kindly ask the usher will show this hard copy to our learned friends from the Prosecution and then to the witness. This version seems to be far more legible. For the record, it is a document of the cabinet of the commander of the General Staff. It is it an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, please have a look at item 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we able to determine - sorry, Madam Vidovic - from the document before the witness the year of the date of this document? Are you able to help us, Mr. Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Must be 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Must be, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see what is typed, but I recognise the date in handwriting. It says: Kakanj, the 26th of February, but I am not certain I can tell you what the year is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we can go to page 2 of the document and then we'll return to the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there is the heading, or the header. It says the 6th of February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, do you see it somewhere? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] you can see another date here, Your Honours, from 1995, it seems. Can we now please go back to page 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, please focus your attention on item 1 where it says that it -- what is ordered is to plan, organise a carry-out training with commanders and Chiefs of Staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was training conducted all the way up to the level corps commanders and Chiefs of Staff of corps in 1995, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask for an Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to show D987 to the witness next. For the record, it is an document of the General Staff of the armed forces of the 1st of February, 1995. The title is: Order for training courses for the SVB and VP.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, have you seen this document before? Did you receive it during the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please comment upon it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the entire page visible on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is an order of the General Staff concerning training of officers and soldiers of the military security service and the military police by conducting courses in Sarajevo that were supposed to last for a month. But that was not the only occasion. Such training was organised on several occasions during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain type of training was organised for this type of cadre.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What cadre?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military security service and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask for an Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to go to D1067 next. For the record and while we're waiting for the document, it is a document of the morale administration of the General Staff of the 19th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please comment, the first paragraph of the document.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff is forwarding to all subordinate units a document of the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, i.e., of the Supreme Command, concerning breaches of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is a sentence in the document. What is stated is that in some previous decisions and documents the soldiers were acquainted with the provisions of the Geneva Conventions. The soldiers being the soldiers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. My question to you is: Were the soldiers of the army of B&H through the corps acquaint the with the regulations contained in the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it took place on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have an Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1345, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, a few questions on a different topic. As the 1st Corps commander, did you ever come across a document termed directive?
